329:A revision does not erase the earlier statement. On 2026-11-06, Alex chose to keep one evidence record for a repeat and add the new source and any missing thesis link. On 2026-11-08 the Step 2 validation showed that keeping only the earlier text discards details a later report adds, such as a guidance condition; Alex then chose to keep each repeat's own text and source inside the stored record's group, without rewriting the original ("A 继续；跑council loop 开始做"; [Step 2 log](step2-validation-2026-11-07/LOG.md) §7). In the judge's ledger each member of a group is its own evidence record, related to the original as the same claim (D204), and the judge reads each copy with that note; a second or later copy of a statement already in the same request is 31% to 34% of what the judge is shown in the saved clean draws (26% to 31% in production's), and how a judgement weighs copies is not tested further (Step 2 log §17). Multiple articles reporting the same statement do not automatically establish independent original sources. The current production writer stores separate repeat records, so this is a change for the clean path and needs implementation and verification; the existing historical records remain available. Step 3 ends when the theses, evidence and relationships are saved. The grouping library (`step3/library.py`, frozen) holds them; a measurement writer (`step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py`) writes them into the judge's ledger together with the judged questions, processing steps, completed days and closings (D429, D564, D567).     14	## 7. Step 4: judge the thesis
    15	
    16	Judgement is separate from reading and saving an item. Saving the revised capital-spending forecast records **what the company said**;
    17	judgement says **what that means for the question**, from all the saved evidence. Alex opened this step's design on 2026-11-10:
    18	"设计新系统自己的“判断”环节" (D396). The full design is [Step 4 design](step4-2026-11-10/DESIGN.md) (version 35); this section states
    19	what it does.
    20	
    21	### Two parts
    22	
    23	1. **The ladder step (Step 4a).** One call per newly opened thesis, after Step 3 has saved the item that opened it and before that
    24	   day's judging. It reads the thesis, the article that opened it, the company and its fiscal-year note, and the list of themes; it
    25	   reads nothing later than the opening article. It writes the judged question, its answer choices and its due day, and lists every
    26	   other part of the thesis as not judged. Model: gpt-6-luna at medium effort.
    27	2. **The judge (Step 4b).** Production's frozen judge (judging-v7, D354), unchanged. Once a day it judges every judged question whose
    28	   evidence changed, citing the evidence it used. On a question's due day production's closing step records the final answer (D567).
    29	
    30	### What the ladder step decides
    31	
    32	- **One judged question per thesis**, the part the thesis's outcome names. Every other part is listed as not judged and shown beside
    33	  the answer (D397). A second side of the same bet is context, not a second question (D436).
    34	- **An event** has at most three outcomes: it happened, it is ruled out, or still open by the due day. Code writes "still open"
    35	  (D409). Ruling out is stated as who decides and what they decide (D416); a proceeding that formally ends without the conclusion
    36	  asked for is ruled out (D420).
    37	- **A figure** has exactly five ranges set against a reference, with the favourable end registered and its reason; code orders and
    38	  labels the ranges (D398, carrying D186). An amount already reported may be the reference, labelled as that and never as the market's
    39	  expectation (D411). Where the texts do not settle it, an amount the company owes or guarantees has the lower end favourable (D413).
    40	- **The owner**: the company, or a theme. A government's permission or ban on a class of product belongs to the theme (D418).
    41	- **The due day**: for an event, a stated date or the last day of the thesis's period (D403); for a year's figure, code sets it to the
    42	  fiscal year-end plus 60 days for a company and the calendar year-end plus 90 days for a theme (D414).
    43	- **A decline** is allowed with its reason: no main part, a rolling twelve months with no publication day (D417), or no theme that
    44	  covers the matter. An answer refused twice by code writes no question (D405). A thesis without a judged question is kept, and the
    45	  links to it are counted, not judged.
    46	
    47	### Where it stands
    48	
    49	- **Built and frozen as it ran in the fourth Stage A** (D426). A second look by the model at its own answer was tested and not adopted
    50	  (D425).
    51	- **Gate 1 (Stage A) is not met.** In the fourth run on Alex's 44 theses, lines 2 and 6 were met, line 5 on two of three readings, and
    52	  lines 1, 3 and 4 missed by 1, 2 and 3 answers of 131. Every later reading on fresh topics also missed it (nine readings in all).
    53	- **Gate 2 (Stage B) is not met.** Three draws, 236 judgements: unsupported figure answers 3.4%, 3.2% and 10.5% against a limit of
    54	  12.7–14.4%, and yes/no answers 0.9%, 0.8% and 4.9% against 5% (both met); the control line could not be exercised (4 comparable
    55	  controls of 8 needed), and the strictest reading of the last-answer line missed (3 of 24)
    56	  ([result](step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/STAGE_B_RESULT.md)). Re-sending the judge cannot close the control shortfall (D576, D592).
    57	- **On the product's page** the judged question, its answer choices and the parts not judged are shown without any invented direction

Otherwise reference is null. value is the number the item states, with value_to its upper end when the item states a range; when the item gives it in words alone, value is null: never supply a number the item does not state. The ranges of a figure state the outcome against a reference that has a value: the middle range holds that value, or runs from at or below a stated range's lower end to at or above its upper end, and the ranges on either side are outcomes above and below it. When reference is null or has no value, the ranges are your own estimate of the outcomes that could happen.
    17	- favourable_end, for a figure about a company: higher when a higher outcome is good for its business, lower when a lower one is, with one sentence why. A result and its direction are separate: capital spending can build capacity or hurt returns. For an amount the company owes, guarantees or has committed to pay, when neither the topic nor the item settles which end is good for the business, because they argue both ends or say nothing on it, it is lower; when the topic's own words say that more of it is good, it is higher. A retailer's lease guarantees that the item says win store sites and also weigh on its credit are lower; an airline's aircraft purchase commitments that the topic tracks as the fleet growth its plan needs are higher. For a theme's figure it is n/a.
    18	
    19	The due day
    20	- Set the due day when the question can be resolved. It falls after the item's day, and on or after the day the material that settles the question is published.
    21	- For a figure, use its publication date, which falls after the end of the period the figure covers: stated when the topic or the item gives it, expected_publication when you set the day you expect it to be published. Company figures use the company's fiscal year: "this year" contains the item's publication day, and "next year" follows it; convert fiscal years using the fiscal-year note.     22	- For an event, name the date at which its outcome is assessed: stated when the topic or the item gives it; period_end when it is the last day of the period the topic names, or the company's current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision that has no date.
    23	- When the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation, the due day is at most 548 days (18 months) after the item: for an obligation already taken on, its next annual filing; for one not yet signed, the day by which the signing can be checked.

item.text:
**The new system is not ready to replace the running pipeline. Gate 1 still fails with Astra, and Gate 2 has not passed.** The clearest Gate 1 problem is that Astra sometimes refuses to write a question even when Alex has already said the topic is one question: for example, total semiconductor sales and the AI-chip portion of that total.

I recommend one next step: **a $0 audit and design of a general explanation of Alex’s existing “two sides of one bet” decision**, using stored examples outside the 44. It must cover both a total and its part, and a figure with a condition. It must also check cases that really are two separate questions. Only if that audit produces a defensible candidate and a sufficiently informative test should the council decide whether to spend on a small comparison.

This is an independent read-only review of the records. I did **not** run a new council, make a model call, or edit the record. The “council” findings below distinguish my conclusions from the earlier recorded discussions.

### 1. Where each gate stands

| Gate | Measured status | What that means |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Answer choices** | **Failed.** Astra’s 132 sends passed lines 1, 3 and 6, but had **7 unjustified refusals** on line 4. Lines 2 and 5 differ under the two treatments of unresolved reader disputes. | The failure does not depend on resolving the deadline disputes: line 4 fails either way. [Astra report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/report-output.txt:1), [D649](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8938) |
| **2. Judge on the new questions** | **Not passed.** All three draws completed and all 26 eligible questions were judged. Figure and yes/no unsupported-answer limits were met. Only **4 comparable controls** had the necessary material, against **8 required**; under the strictest reading, **3 of 24** final answers were unsupported, above the one-in-ten limit. | The control test is **unexercised**, not a demonstrated failure of all other questions. The 236 daily judgements repeat questions and are not 236 independent tests. This was measured on the earlier Luna answer choices, not an accepted Astra configuration. [Stage B result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/STAGE_B_RESULT.md:1) |
| **3. End-to-end comparison** | **Owed.** The required comparison and a numerical definition of “beats” remain open. Earlier comparisons are diagnostics, not acceptance. | No evidence yet establishes that the complete new system beats the running one. [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:126) |
| **4. Use on unseen news** | **Not an accepted gate yet.** One fresh-week diagnostic covered **2 of 5** major matters and had **6 of 7** last answers supported, versus **10 of 15** for the other system; its proposed limits are not Alex’s accepted limits. | This small diagnostic is a warning, not a final comparison or an accepted gate result. [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:394) |
| **5. Integration and release** | **Incomplete.** Some integration has been built and tested, but the full production path and release acceptance remain owed. | It cannot make up for the preceding gates. I have not reviewed or proposed further work on pages or live service. [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:126) |

For Gate 2 specifically, the figure unsupported rates were **3/88, 3/95 and 10/95**, each below its respective baseline-plus-five-point limit; yes/no rates were **1/117, 1/122 and 6/122**, all within 5%. The strict final-answer result was **3/24**, with two “insufficient” answers reported separately. [Stage B result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/STAGE_B_RESULT.md:12)

### 2. Astra Gate 1: accounting and disputed cases

**The seven refusals are real misses under the recorded reading.** They comprise three refusals of HBM shipment growth with a shortage condition, three of total semiconductor revenue with its AI-chip portion, and one of combined HBM capacity with a timing condition. The report gives **26 justified and 7 unjustified refusals out of 33**. [Astra report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/report-output.txt:20), [D649](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8955)

Alex already settled the first two shapes. He answered **“算一个题，第三处不改”**—count it as one question—and the resulting decision explicitly names “the shortage beside the shipments” and “the AI-chip share beside the chip total” as second sides of one bet, kept as context and shown as not judged. That supports asking the main question in these named cases; it does **not** establish a universal rule that every total always takes priority over every part. The capacity case also needs its own topic-specific reading rather than a blanket rule. [D436](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4847)

The two accounting treatments are:

- **Unresolved points counted in Astra’s favour:** line 2 passes; line 5 passes with **40 of 44 right**, including **31 with written choices**.
- **Unresolved points counted against Astra:** line 2 misses by **one**; line 5 has **35 of 44 right**, but only **26 with written choices**, below the required 28.
- Line 6 passes in both treatments: the favourable direction agrees for all **9** applicable topics, and the due day agrees for **32 of 33** applicable topics. Consistency does not establish that a due day is correct. [Astra report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/report-output.txt:1)

The disputed points are **not all one unresolved owner decision**:

1. **Annual-figure deadlines: the instrument is internally ambiguous.** The reader form says a year’s figure with no stated publication day takes the code-set date, “**60 days after the company’s fiscal year-end**”; its detailed deadline mark also says an existing obligation “**is due at its next annual filing**.” [Reader brief](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md:68), [deadline mark](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md:98)

   D414 says for a **one-year figure** whose date would otherwise be estimated, code sets fiscal year-end plus 60 days; “**A day the topic or the item states is kept**.” Alex accepted code setting it. Where the disputed answer really is a year-end figure and no exact publication day is stated, D414 supports the code-set day, not an approximate February date substituted by a reader. [D414](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4568)

   The third readers demonstrate the collision: one failed an April 1 date because the filing was around February; the other held it because no exact filing day was stated and April 1 was the code-set date. [Codex ruling](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/third-reader/rulings-codex-1.jsonl:1), [Claude ruling](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/third-reader/rulings-claude-1.jsonl:1)

2. **A stated event deadline is separately governed by D403.** Alex chose “**保持更严**”: use the date in the topic or article, or the last day of the topic’s period; the model chooses no other day. That settles the rule for an event, but applying it still requires deciding what that particular topic asks and which period it names. [D403](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4414)

3. **The other disagreements must not be silently converted into deadline rulings.** For example, the two third readers split over whether an omitted Nvidia spending share was already adequately described in the unjudged-parts list. They also split on whether a 2027 or 2028 shipping deadline followed the topic. Those are different questions from the annual-filing conflict. [Codex rulings](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/third-reader/rulings-codex-3.jsonl:1), [Claude rulings](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/third-reader/rulings-claude-3.jsonl:1)

The fourth Luna reading had line 1 missed by **1**, line 3 by **2**, and line 4 by **3** on the favourable treatment; its stricter treatment had **5, 4 and 3** respectively. This makes Astra’s recorded improvement on lines 1 and 3 useful evidence, but Astra is worse on the seven recorded refusals, and this is not a controlled production comparison. [Luna report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/result-4/report.txt:1), [Astra report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-ladder-stage-a-astra-2026-11-17/run-1/report-output.txt:1)

### 3. What the latest diagnostic shows

The D651 test compared the unchanged Astra request with the same request plus two sentences derived from D436. There were **11 topics, two sends per version**, for **44 sends and $1.49**. The two readers had classified **six topics as questions** and **five as justified refusals** before seeing the answers. [D651](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8991), [classifications](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/score-output.txt:1)

Only **two** of the six target topics actually exercised the refusal problem in the unchanged version, below the pre-set minimum of **three**, so the registered result is **inconclusive**:

- On **pool-7**, the unchanged version refused twice; the edited version wrote two questions that neither reader marked faulty.
- On **pool-17**, both versions refused twice. The edited version did not recover the total-and-split question.
- All five justified-refusal controls held in the edited version.
- The strict topic-level accounting flagged pool-17 as worse on the agreed count: **two** edited failures versus **one** unchanged failure. One unchanged refusal was disputed, so this is a reader-count difference, not proof that the edit changed the written behaviour. [Score](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/score-output.txt:63), [per-topic results](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/score-output.txt:110), [round 44](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/challenge-44.md:5)

This is **a promising observed recovery on one topic**, not proof that the sentences fix all “figure plus condition” cases. Likewise, the failure on one total-and-split topic is evidence against assuming that class is fixed, not proof that every such case will fail. The prediction that a new Gate 1 run would still miss by three or four is plausible, but it is a prediction, not a measured result. The pre-set rule correctly stops the gate rerun. [D652](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9020), [test rule](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/second_side_probe.py:227)

The model comparisons also do not establish a cheap substitute. Sol improved agreed failures from **13 to 5 of 78**, but exceeded the refusal bound. The paired Astra screens recorded **4 of 78** agreed failures, with the complementary screen closing under its own rule. Opus and DeepSeek each had only one draw per model and were inconclusive; Luna itself moved from **7 to 1** agreed failures between those one-draw trials. [Sol result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/model/RESULT.md:3), [Astra result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/astra/RESULT-REST.md:10), [Opus](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/opus/RESULT.md:1), [DeepSeek](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/deepseek/RESULT.md:1)

### 4. Production blockers, in order

1. **Gate 1 is failed and the written questions also need substantive scrutiny.** The seven Astra refusals alone block the gate. Separately, a source-backed review found **11 material issues in 51 Astra-written questions**: four signed-deal completion dates, three events due before their settling report, three widened periods, and one invented measure. These are not 11 independent topics, and the later Rubin trace attributes its widened period to the topic’s own period field. They show why a zero hard-line count would not alone establish usable questions. [Astra review](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/astra-review/RESULT.md:1), [D638](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8687)

2. **Gate 2 lacks enough comparable controls and has a strict final-answer miss.** A repeat send of the same judge cannot manufacture four more comparable questions with the required material. Gate 1 must produce usable, comparable questions and allow the relevant evidence to reach the judge; even then, the final-answer quality needs to be measured. The judge’s internals are outside this review. [Stage B result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/STAGE_B_RESULT.md:79), [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:440)

3. **The later gates remain owed**, including an agreed comparison standard for Gate 3 and an accepted Gate 4. They are not the next work in this review’s scope. [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:126)

4. **Cost at the requested scale is unknown.** The stored November 13 clean run charged **$0.028, $0.029 and $0.047** for the three Luna answer-choice components; Astra’s screens averaged roughly **$0.037–$0.050 per send**, and the Astra Gate 1 run cost **$4.74**. Alex’s concern about 1,000 asset categories cannot be answered from one NVDA period: the number of new questions, article volume, overlap and retries at that scale are unknown. A simple cost per question is useful for budgeting, not a production forecast. [Spend file](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13/spend-by-component.json:29), [Opus cost comparison](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/opus/RESULT.md:52), [D649](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8938)

**Authority:** Alex chose Astra as the candidate and authorized the recorded Gate 1 launch; that choice does not waive the gates. Under D439, when he is inactive the council may reach and record reversible decisions, including opening a new version of this frozen step. It cannot change the frozen ruler, exceed the applicable spending authority, or deploy, publish, push or commit without being asked. A new frozen-ruler version remains Alex’s decision. The recorded $40 ceiling was Claude’s limit for that period, not a figure Alex personally set; later explicitly authorized spending must be accounted for separately. [D648](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8914), [D439](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4871), [D544](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6616)

Alex may of course settle genuinely open product questions himself. The council should not describe every question as “only Alex can decide” when D439 delegates reversible choices, nor treat its own interpretation as an Alex decision.

### 5. One next step, then the step after it

**Next: a $0, read-only source and request audit of the D436 candidate.** Compare the full request, schema and closing check with D436 and the stored topics: the two recovered/refused diagnostic topics, true separate-question controls, and the named total-and-part and shortage cases. Produce a general, cross-domain candidate only if the existing decision supports its boundary. In the same audit, resolve the reader-form conflict against D403 and D414 for each applicable case, without changing the frozen gold or retroactively declaring a pass.

- **Falsifier:** the proposed wording would make a genuinely separate question disappear, change a justified refusal into an unsound question, conflict with the existing request or decisions, or has no outside cases capable of testing the intended failure. Any of these stops that candidate.
- **Cost:** **$0 in model calls**; the cost is reviewer time. No model send is part of this step.
- **What changes the plan:** if a source review shows the alleged recovery chose an unsupported measure, if the broader rule would merge separate bets, or if there are too few suitable outside cases, do not spend on that candidate. Return the unresolved boundary to the council with the examples and choose the cheaper reversible course. The earlier cold reviewer specifically warned that pool-7’s DDR4 choice needed source checking before calling it a confirmed recovery. [Round 43 review](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/codex-challenge-43.md:1)

**After that:** if the audit survives, have the council pre-register and price a **small matched comparison outside the 44**, with enough independently classified target cases, justified-refusal controls, both reader countings, and source review of every recovered question. A positive small test would justify considering a Gate 1 rerun; it would not itself pass the gate. The 44 have already informed the proposed repair, so any rerun on them must be labelled an **exposed acceptance set**, followed by fresh-material evidence before generalizing. [Round 40 review](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/codex-challenge-40.md:3)

### 6. Errors and overclaims in the record

- **“The two sentences fix” a class is too strong.** D652’s heading and round 44 say the edit fixes a figure-plus-condition shape. The registered result is inconclusive, with only one recovered topic and two sends. The narrower statement is that it recovered pool-7 in this diagnostic. [D652](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9020), [score](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/score-output.txt:242)

- **The diagnostic’s population description is inaccurate.** D651 says the 11 topics came from the 48 outside both the 44 and the 26, but its own topic file identifies **three as `26-set`**. They remain outside the 44, but they are not all outside the earlier 26. [D651](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8999), [topic list](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-7/topics-11.json:42)

- **The decision page overstates the reader-control conclusion.** “The readers are not too harsh” goes beyond the reference test: the control found no confirmed reader error under its rule, but the careful writer had **four of 26** faults when unresolved points were counted against it. It does not prove the readers’ thresholds are generally correct. [Decision page](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-16.md:125), [D624](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8405)

- **The request contains a real deadline conflict.** It requires the due day to be “on or after” publication of settling material, but also sets an event at the end of its period. Those can be different days. Its blanket next-filing instruction for obligations also reaches completion events, while D403 governs event dates. This matters downstream: a consistent date can still close a question before the evidence arrives. [Request](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/candidate-system.txt:19), [source review](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/astra-review/RESULT.md:10)

- **The PRD is stale on the selected model.** It still says the step uses Luna, while D648 records Alex’s later choice of Astra for the candidate. The decision page also still describes the Astra gate launch as unsent. These are historical documents, but a reader using them as current status would be misled. [PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:338), [decision page](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-16.md:166), [D648](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8914)

- **“Reasoning effort is not the lever” is broader than the experiment.** On this request and 26 topics, medium and high produced **13 and 14** agreed failed sends out of 78; the registered comparison closes. It does not establish that reasoning effort cannot help another request or population. [Effort result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-6/effort/RESULT.md:10)

The immediate decision is therefore to diagnose and audit the known refusal mechanism at no API cost, while preserving the failed result and the unresolved measurement disputes. The record does not yet support claiming that the edited request, Astra, or the complete system is production-ready.
